translations.backTranslation: Microsoft Foundry Managed Compute: Private Endpoint Verified by Actual Testing

This repository answers only one question: After shutting down public network access for the associated Foundry resource, can the business client still deploy the GlobalManagedCompute model via a Private Endpoint? In a test in an independent environment, calls outside the VNet changed from 200 to 403, while calls within the VNet remained at 200; after restoring the original value, calls outside the VNet returned 200.

Conclusion boundary: This test only verifies the inbound network path from the client to the inference endpoint; It does not prove that the managed computed Pod is located in the client's VNet, nor does it prove that outbound traffic passes through the client's VNet; It also does not prove that prompt or completion has zero retention, nor does it prove that the preview capability has met production requirements.

Running scripts requires Python 3.11+ and only uses the Python standard library. Online reproduction also requires Azure CLI and a credential to call model deployment: either the API key for Foundry resources or Entra identity, either of both.

The execution order must not be reversed: first prove that the private network path is available, then close the public network. Otherwise, if DNS or routing is mismatched, operators themselves will be locked out of the network.
Stage — client location — public network access — the result that must be seen
1 — Associate VNet outside — Open — Chat Completions request returns 200
2 — Associate within VNet — Enable — DNS resolution to private addresses and return 200
3 — Associate outside VNet — Close — Return 403 Public access is disabled
4 — Associate within VNet — Close — DNS still resolves to private addresses and returns 200
5 — Associate outside VNet — Restore original value — If the original value is Enabled, request to return 200
Completion condition: The Foundry resource returns to the public network access state saved before testing, and all five stages of public and private network results meet expectations.
What are the responsibilities of the platform and the customer?
Microsoft Foundry and Azure provide — customer responsibility and acceptance
GlobalManagedCompute model deployment and its affiliated Foundry resources — independent non-production foundry resources; All projects under it must be disposable test assets
Public network access settings for the resource — Contributor permissions for Foundry resources; Save the original value before modification, and read back to confirm after modification
The connection group is the Private Endpoint for accounts—Private Endpoint private subnet, Network Contributor permissions, and the status of Approved and Succeeded connections
Private DNS Zone Integration — Requires a private DNS zone, VNet link, or DNS forwarding, and confirms client resolution to a private address

Data Face Authentication: API key (api-key request header) or Entra token (Authorization: Bearer) — the same credential is used throughout all five stages; If the resource is set to disableLocalAuth=true, only Entra can be used
Azure Container Instances (ACI) can be used to perform probing — delegated workload subnets, credentials passed in via ARM secureValue, evidence preserved, and a cleanup leader assigned

Benefit: After shutting down the public network, neither the model URL nor the deployment itself needs to be changed. Cost: Every client must be able to route to VNet, and DNS must resolve the model URL into the private address of the Private Endpoint. Network control is the responsibility of the foundry resources, not on individual Managed Compute model deployments.

Private Endpoint carries real inference requests — the same probe source code is executed in ACI with a private IP; Before and after shutting down the public network, DNS resolves to RFC 1918 private addresses, and Chat Completions return 200. The evidence only covers *.services.ai.azure.com routes belonging to the Foundry resource, so it is unclear whether Managed Compute also exposes other inbound hostnames.
Five-stage real-world testing

During testing, Foundry resources, model deployment, inference endpoints, credentials, and request content are fixed, only changing the client's network location and the public network access settings for the Foundry resources.

This test uses the Entra token because the test resource disabled key access (disableLocalAuth=true). Foundry resources support both types of authentication: API-key request heading API key or Authorization: Bearer passing Entra token. Scripts support both. Public access is a resource-level network configuration and is independent of which credential the client uses; However, this time only Entra was tested.

Private network probing uses ACI, assigning private IPs in the dedicated workload subnet associated with VNet, then sending HTTPS requests to private addresses resolved by DNS; It is not Azure Bastion. Both ACI probes use the same probe_endpoint.py source code, with exit codes of 0. Public evidence does not store generated content or parsed IPs; Request IDs only retain the SHA-256 summary. Probe timestamps only prove execution order and do not represent delay distribution.

The automatically generated call log is the only machine-read-through entry point for five stages. Source of evidence records explain which fields come from probes, which fingerprints are derived after runtime, and how to retrieve the probe source code actually executed in the 762b6978 submission.

Verification principle
Hierarchy — Actual implementation — Conditions — Evidence boundary

DNS — resolve_addresses resolve the endpoint, classify_addresses divide all addresses into public, private, or mixed networks — VNet client outputs dnsClass=private — evidence has been preserved, but the resolution address has not been reconciled item-by-item with the private endpoint network card address

How clients access Private Endpoints

The key is not whether the client is a VM or a container, but whether both conditions are met: the route can reach the VNet where the Private Endpoint resides; DNS can resolve the same model URL into the private address of the Private Endpoint.
Client location — network path — DNS requirements
VM, ACI, and Kubernetes workloads within the same or peer VNet—routing or VNet peering—link the same set of Foundry Private DNS Zones to each client VNet, or run a unified enterprise DNS parser
Local data center applications—ExpressRoute or Site-to-Site VPNs—forward Foundry service domain terms to the inbound endpoint of Azure DNS Private Resolver or the DNS forwarder within Azure
Developer computers — point-to-site VPN or VM logging into VNet via Azure Bastion — using DNS provided by VPN/resolver; Bastion is just one way during development and not a required component

Based on: Azure Private Endpoint DNS integration scenario and Azure DNS Private Resolver. The ACI in this repository is only a one-time authentication execution end and does not represent what the production client should look like.
Recommended configuration for production environments
Below are suggestions based on official documentation and this differential test; this configuration itself was not tested in this test.
Hierarchy — Recommended configuration — Reason

Foundry resources — keep publicNetworkAccess=Disabled; Do not use the IP whitelist for the "selected network" as the production access path — the 403 in the test is caused by this setup; The IP whitelist is equivalent to opening a new public path

Private Endpoint location — using a hub-spoke topology, create a Private Endpoint for each Foundry resource in the hub VNet (or shared service spoke) — all peer spoke can access it; unless required by isolation policies, it is not necessary to create one separately for each application

Application VNet — connects to the hub via VNet peering; Production clients are workloads already in spoke (AKS, App Service, Functions, VMs with VNet integration) — peering provides routing; the type of client doesn't matter

Azure internal DNS — link three Foundry Private DNS Zones (privatelink.cognitiveservices.azure.com, privatelink.openai.azure.com, privatelink.services.ai.azure.com) to the hub; speak points uniformly to the central DNS (Azure DNS Private Resolver inbound endpoint or custom DNS forwarder), or links the same group of zones to each spoke — each client must resolve the model URL into a Private Endpoint address

Local Data Center — Access hub via ExpressRoute private peer or site-to-site VPN; Forward these three zone conditions to the Private Resolver inbound endpoint — the local DNS server cannot see Azure Private DNS Zone
Developers and operations personnel — point-to-site VPN access hub, or logging into the Stepping Board VM via Azure Bastion — Bastion for use and does not carry application traffic

Credentials — API keys are stored in Azure Key Vault and rotated regularly, or managed with inference roles; Choose based on the team's key management strategy — both inference endpoints are supported; network isolation is independent of which type is chosen
Change control — run from spoke once before and after each network or DNS change probe_endpoint.py — do phase 2 before phase 3 to avoid locking yourself out

Azure Container Instances and Azure Bastion are only validation tools and operations entry points in this repository, not production data paths. References: Hub-spoke Network Topology, Private Endpoint DNS Integration,
Azure OpenAI authentication methods, disable local authentication.
Common misconceptions
Misunderstandings — what the code and evidence show
"The Private Endpoint replicates a private model." — The model deployment and URL remain unchanged; The Foundry resource belongs only to which network path leads to the model.

"DNS returns a private address, indicating that the Managed Compute Pod is in the client's VNet." — The probe only proves that the client has resolved to the private address and received a valid response, but does not indicate where the Pod is located.

"Only ACI can access the private network model." — ACI is just the execution side used in this test. Any client with private network routing, private DNS, and valid credentials (API key or Entra identity) can call it.

What does this set of data indicate, and what does it not indicate:
Running Private Endpoint doesn't slow down. TTFT p50 drops from about 0.5–0.8 seconds to about 0.2–0.4 seconds, and p95 in every gear

More convergent. A reasonable explanation for this difference is that ACI is deployed in the same region (Japaneast), while workstations access the public network from overseas; It reflects "same-region client vs. remote client," not the acceleration of Private Link itself.
The decoding speed for both paths for a single request is exactly the same (about 40 tok/s for concurrent 1, about 36 tok/s for concurrent 64): this figure is determined by the model
The decision has nothing to do with the internet.

Saturation point above 64, but it was not measured this time.

Repeat the steps

All the following commands use Bash. Resource and deployment commands are executed on the control end equipped with Azure CLI; Public probes run outside the associated VNet; Private probes run on authorized probe execution ends in the independent workload subnet. Each probe executor must obtain this repository. The private probe executor requires Python 3.11+, DNS associated with VNet, TCP 443 outbound connection to inference endpoints, and credentials passed in through the process environment: AZURE_AI_API_KEY (resource API key) or AZURE_ACCESS_TOKEN (Entra token); If neither is present, the probe calls the Azure CLI to obtain the token. All five phases must use the same credentials, inference endpoints, model deployment, prompts, and token caps.

Azure prerequisites: independent, non-production foundry resources, with all projects being disposable test assets; Azure public cloud; Contributor to the affiliated foundry resources; Network Contributor for target VNets and subnets; To create a Private DNS Zone, a Private DNS Zone Contributor or equivalent permissions must also be present. Private Endpoint private subnets must already exist. The application or network leader is responsible for temporary detection of the execution end's lifecycle and cleanup.

Testing

Testing does not require Azure credentials, GPUs, or online inference endpoints. Coverage includes URL and DNS classification, authentication response semantics, ACI only created, no overriding, zero PATCH denial path, original value restoration, evidence variation, bilingual reader flow, Azure Translator evidence, and Level 5 rule contracts.
Completion conditions: All tests passed, derivation evidence matches the source file, and output REPO_VALIDATION=PASS.
